The Narmada Valley Development Project, which envisaged the construction of 30 major, 135 medium, and some 3,000 minor dams on the Narmada river flowing through Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, and Maharashtra, sparked the longest-running anti-dam movement in modern history: the Narmada Bachao Andolan (NBA). questionText: Right-wing critics (such as the Swatantra Party) criticized the planning model for creating a:

options.text: System that paid too much money to private farmers
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: 'License-Permit-Quota Raj' that stifled private initiative and fostered corruption and inefficiency
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Right Critique Mixed Economy.

options.text: Monarchy dominated by the British governor-general
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Pure communist society without any private businesses
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Politics of Planned Development (Right Critique Mixed Economy):
'License-Permit-Quota Raj' that stifled private initiative and fostered corruption and inefficiency

Detailed Analysis:
Right-wing economists and businessmen argued that state bureaucratic controls, industrial licenses, and import quotas bred red-tapism and corruption.
Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.
